production.note: US model years. First: MBUSA, "The new 2025 Mercedes-AMG GT 63 S E PERFORMANCE" (coupe). Still on sale: mbusa.com lists the 2027 model (inventory link "year=2027"; page title says 2026) (mbusa-gt63-se-coupe-2027). The four-door AMG GT 63 S E Performance (X290) is a different car and not part of this record.

body.note: Sold as the "AMG GT 63 S E PERFORMANCE Coupe"; "Passenger capacity 2 (4 optional)". C/D panel: "2+2-passenger, 2-door hatchback".

configuration.note: "Handcrafted AMG 4.0L V8 biturbo w/rear 150kW electric motor".

displacementL.note: "4.0L"; the C/D panel also says "4.0-liter" (cd-amg-gt63-se-2025). No cc figure was given on the pages opened.

aspiration.note: "V8 biturbo"; panel: "twin-turbocharged and intercooled DOHC 32-valve 4.0-liter V-8".

fuel.note: Panel: "5-kWh lithium-ion; peak charge rate, AC 3.7 kW" (chargeable from the grid). MBUSA: "400-volt, 6.1kWh AMG High Performance Battery" (mbusa-2025-gt63-se).

drivetrain.note: "Drive configuration AMG Performance 4MATIC+ all-wheel drive". The C/D panel says "rear/all-wheel-drive" (4MATIC+ can run rear-drive only).

transmission.note: "Automatic transmission AMG SPEEDSHIFT® MCT 9-speed" (recorded as Automatic as in the other AMG MCT records). The rear electric motor has its own two-speed gearbox (panel: "Transmissions, F/R: 9-speed automatic/2-speed automatic").

powerHp.note: Combined system output. Quote (mbusa.com, 2027 model): "805 hp @ 5,500-6,500 rpm". Same at launch: MBUSA 2025 page, "Together, this system delivers 805 horsepower, 1,047 lb-ft of torque" (mbusa-2025-gt63-se); C/D panel: "(combined output: 805 hp, 1047 lb-ft; 5-kWh lithium-ion; peak charge rate, AC 3.7 kW)" (cd-amg-gt63-se-2025).

weightLb.note: Manufacturer US curb weight (weight-order step 1), 2027 model, 9-speed MCT (the only transmission). Quote (mbusa.com): "Curb weight 4,850 lbs"; no estimate label. Step 1 outranks the Car and Driver road-test curb weight of the 2025 car (4,743 lb, cd-amg-gt63-se-2025), which is listed in discrepancies. No MBUSA weight for 2025 or 2026 was found, so the reference year is 2027 (805 hp unchanged since 2025), as in the C 63 S E Performance record.
